coverage_note: General municipal employees (local government and school district employees who are not public safety or transit employees) under the Municipal Employment Relations Act, Wis. Stat. 111.70 to 111.77, as amended by 2011 Wis. Act 10, administered by the Wisconsin Employment Relations Commission. Public safety and transit employees keep broader bargaining and arbitration rights, and state employees are under subchapter V; neither is covered cell by cell here.

governing_statute.value: Municipal Employment Relations Act, Wis. Stat. 111.70 to 111.77 (as amended by 2011 Wis. Act 10)
governing_statute.quote: Municipal employees have the right of self-organization, and the right to form, join, or assist labor organizations, to bargain collectively through representatives of their own choosing

who_may_bargain.value: Municipal employees other than independent contractors, supervisors, and confidential, managerial or executive employees; a general municipal employee unit's representative must win an annual WERC recertification election
who_may_bargain.quote: b. Annually, the commission shall conduct an election to certify the representative of the collective bargaining unit that contains a general municipal employee.

scope_of_bargaining.value: Total base wages only, with increases capped by the consumer price index change unless approved by referendum; all other conditions of employment are prohibited subjects; agreements last one year
scope_of_bargaining.quote: The municipal employer is prohibited from bargaining collectively with a collective bargaining unit containing a general municipal employee with respect to any of the following: 1. Any factor or condition of employment except wages, which includes only total base wages and excludes any other compensation

impasse_procedure.value: Mediation only: WERC mediates on request or on its own initiative, without power of compulsion; no interest arbitration for general municipal employees
impasse_procedure.quote: The commission or its designee shall function as mediator in labor disputes involving general municipal employees upon request of one or both of the parties, or upon initiation of the commission. The function of the mediator shall be to encourage voluntary settlement by the parties. No mediator has the power of compulsion.

strike_legality.value: Prohibited for municipal employees and labor organizations
strike_legality.quote: Nothing contained in this subchapter constitutes a grant of the right to strike by any municipal employee or labor organization, and such strikes are hereby expressly prohibited.

agency_fee_status.value: Not permitted for general municipal employees: fair-share agreements are allowed only for public safety and transit employees, and Janus v. AFSCME (2018) bars agency fees from nonconsenting public employees
agency_fee_status.quote: but the prohibition shall not apply to a fair-share agreement that covers public safety employees or transit employees.
